packs.title: Garden Roofs and Stone
packs.promise: Find house lines, stone creatures and garden shapes beyond the harbour walk.

q.s: Collect a small creature’s curves without needing a sighting.
st: Find a stone frog figure visible from a permitted path, or use the operator’s Artificial Lake gallery photograph showing stone frogs.
Collect three shapes from one figure: a raised eye, a rounded body and a bent leg. Draw or describe only what you can see.
Arrange your discoveries from sharpest-looking to softest-looking. Save your order and explain one choice without touching the stone.

q.s: Write a miniature exchange between two shapes.
st: Observe the square from a suitable permitted viewpoint, or use the operator’s Olympic Square photograph.
Choose a curved paving line and a straight column as two imagined speakers. Write four short lines: the curve speaks, the column replies, the curve changes its idea, and the column answers.
Give your exchange a title and identify it as an imagined conversation. Keep it on paper; no public performance or physical pose is needed.

q.s: Collect a crossing, a border and a change of texture.
st: Choose a ground chessboard visible from a permitted edge, or use the operator’s Chess Garden photograph. Leave any players and their space undisturbed.
Collect one crossing of lines, one outer border and one change between pale and darker paving textures. Observe from outside rather than walking across a board.
Arrange the discoveries from smallest visible detail to broadest shape. Save the order as a three-part sketch or note.

packs.title: Harbour Lines and Small Scenes
packs.promise: Collect the waterfront’s curves, write a little scene and keep a harbour moment of your own.

q.t: A Wall Made of Small Waves
q.s: Collect three ways a façade catches the light.
st: Choose a comfortable public view of the museum façade, clear of doors, queues and service routes.
Find a repeated panel edge, a rectangle of glass and a narrow shadow between surfaces.
Compare their shapes: which feels most like a line, a window or a small wave? The names are yours to choose.
Save the three details and the comparison you liked best.

q.s: Follow a curve, a grid and a rounded edge.
st: Choose a comfortable place on an open public path beside a curved trellis, with space for others to pass.
Find a long curve in the metal ribs, a repeated opening in the overhead grid and a rounded edge of the planter.
Arrange the three shapes from smallest to largest as they appear from your viewpoint. You can observe from outside the shade.
Save your ordered collection without touching the structure or plants.

q.s: Give a wide view a very small caption.
st: Stop comfortably behind the waterfront barrier and choose a view of water and the opposite skyline.
Pick one water detail and one building shape. They can be as simple as a pale ripple and a tall rectangle.
Write a caption of exactly six words that brings your two details together. Any mood is welcome.
Count the words once and save the caption with the details that began it.
